headline: High risk: shared MCP and broad workspace access create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict pathways; compliance mismatch is also plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Nullclaw can read/write workspace files, use MCP, run browsers, and handle webhooks; OpenBBTerminal also uses MCP servers and a connect-once-consume-everywhere pattern. That creates a default pathway for attacker-controlled content from one agent to influence the other through shared MCP or files, with no provenance controls shown. Uncertainty remains, so I choose the higher severity.
conditions: IF the two agents share an MCP server or workspace path, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF either agent parses the other's file or MCP output as instructions, the attack path is active.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints between the agents.
Separate workspace directories and mount them read-only where possible.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.
Require manual approval for any instruction-like content from the other agent.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering on MCP/file inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, conversation history, and workspace files, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and can use MCP/REST APIs. If they share a workspace or MCP bridge, sensitive data can flow from A into B's outputs or network calls. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem tree, leakage is reachable.
IF OpenBBTerminal receives Nullclaw workspace files through MCP or REST, sensitive content can be exposed.
mitigations: Keep separate OS users and home directories.
Remove shared mounts between the agents.
Block MCP access to secrets-bearing directories.
Review outbound requests from OpenBBTerminal for accidental payload forwarding.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any cross-agent handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Nullclaw has filesystem write, git modification, shell, and broad egress; OpenBBTerminal has MCP and REST APIs and supports multiple instances. If both are attached to the same mutable repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git state changes can race and corrupt state. Because the profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces and no locking, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering is possible.
IF both agents modify the same git repository without locks, branch or index corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize git operations with a lock file.
Make shared resources read-only for one agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Nullclaw can generate web, webhook, and workspace outputs, and OpenBBTerminal exposes APIs and MCP servers that may consume upstream results. That makes it plausible for B to treat A's output as authoritative and propagate mistakes into financial workflows. The profiles do not show explicit verification or downstream action authority, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests Nullclaw-produced text or files without validation, errors can cascade.
IF Nullclaw writes webhook payloads that OpenBBTerminal later consumes, false facts can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before B consumes A's outputs.
Require schema validation on all handoffs.
Mark A's outputs as untrusted by default.
Log source provenance on every transferred artifact.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Nullclaw explicitly touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, service-account JSON, conversation history, audit logs, and webhook payloads, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. That combination raises a plausible compliance mismatch around retention, logging, and sensitive-data handling, even though residency and certifications are not specified. Uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is mixed with Nullclaw audit logs or conversation history, retention obligations may diverge.
IF either agent stores secrets or licensed data in a shared workspace, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Separate regulated and non-regulated datasets.
Disable verbose logging for sensitive sessions.
Set short retention on shared artifacts.
Review data-processing agreements before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing and retention.
